enabled.description: Enable the DateTime indicator applet in the system panel.

clock_format.description: Custom clock format using strftime directives (e.g., '%H:%M'). Leave empty for default.

clock_use_24h.description: Display time in 24-hour format (true) vs 12-hour with AM/PM (false).

clock_show_seconds.description: Show seconds in the clock display when supported by the format.

clock_show_date.description: Display the current date below the time in the clock area.

calendar_enabled.description: Enable the calendar popup when clicking the DateTime indicator.

calendar_show_events.description: Show upcoming events from the system’s default calendar.

calendar_max_events.description: Maximum number of upcoming events to display in the calendar popup.

clock_timezone_mode.description: Timezone display mode: current local time ('local'), home timezone ('home'), or both ('both').

clock_home_timezone.description: Home timezone (e.g., 'Europe/London' or 'America/New_York'). Required when mode is 'home' or 'both'.

calendar_date_format.description: strftime format for dates in the calendar view (e.g., '%A, %B %d' → 'Monday, January 15').

calendar_time_format.description: strftime format for event times in the calendar view (e.g., '%H:%M' → '14:30').

event_sources.description: Additional calendar event sources (e.g., iCal files or webcal feeds). Each entry defines a custom source.

type.description: Source type: 'file' for local iCal, 'webcal' for web-based calendar feeds.

name.description: Display name for this calendar source (e.g., 'Work', 'Family').

url_or_path.description: File path for local calendars (e.g., '/home/user/calendar.ics') or Webcal URL (e.g., 'webcal://example.com/cal.ics').

calendar_show_weather.description: Show current weather forecast in the calendar popup (requires weather-indicator service).

weather_location_id.description: Weather location identifier (e.g., OpenWeatherMap City ID). Required when weather is enabled.

weather_units.description: Temperature and wind units: 'metric' (°C, m/s) or 'imperial' (°F, mph).
